Hon'ble Shri Justice Sanjay Kumar Jaiswal

Judgment on Board
 (09.05.2024)
1.

This appeal has been preferred by the Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor
Vehicles Act, challenging the award dated 27.07.2015 passed by 5th Additional Motor Accident
Claims Tribunal, Bilaspur (C.G.) in Claim Case No. 121/2014, whereby the Tribunal has awarded
compensation of Rs.4,75,800/- with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of application till its
realization, in favour of the claimants for their irreparable loss.

2. The facts, in brief, necessary for disposal of the present appeal, are that on 18.03.2013 at about
05:00 p.m., deceased Uttam @ Rajesh Sahu and Baldev Prasad Kewat were coming from Kotsagar
to their house at Belghana on motorcycle bearing Registration No.C.G.-10/EJ-2699 (for
convenience sake, hereinafter referred as "M-1"). It is alleged that when they reached near Ganesh
Rice Mill, Gobripat on Lormi-Kota main road, another motorcycle bearing Registration
No.C.G.-10/N.A.- 4391 (hereinafter referred as "M-2") driven by Mahettar @ Bakra Sawra in rash
and negligent manner dashed their motorcycle, as a result of which, Uttam @ Rajesh Sahu & Baldev
Kewat sustained grievous injuries and Baldev Prasad Kewat died on the spot whereas Uttam @
Rajesh Sahu died during the course of treatment in Cims Hospital, Bilaspur.
3.

The claimants who are the wife, children and parents of deceased Uttam @ Rajesh Sahu preferred
an application before the Tribunal against insurance company (appellant) & wife of Neutral Citation
2024:Cghc:16965 Mahettar (Sadhna Bai respondent no.8) claiming compensation of
Rs.10,38,000/-.

Learned Tribunal, after considering the evidence and documents available on
record

, awarded total compensation of Rs.4,75,800/- with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date
of application till its realization, in favour of the claimants.

While passing the impugned award, the
Tribunal has fastened the liability of payment of compensation only upon the Insurance Company of
M-2 which was being driven by Mahettar @ Bakra Sawra, therefore, the present appeal has been
filed seeking for exoneration of the insurance company from its liability.

Since M-2
was being driven in violation of insurance policy conditions at the time of accident, the insurance
company cannot be held liable for payment of compensation.

(ii) When the Tribunal itself has not been able to arrive at a conclusion on what basis the driver of M-2 has been held negligent, the Insurance Company of M-2 cannot be held liable for payment of entire compensation and prayed for issuance of an order of 50% liability of the Insurance Company considering it a case of contributory negligence.

5. On the other hand, it has been argued on behalf of learned counsel appearing for the claimants i.e.
respondents 1 to 7 that in the facts and circumstances of the case, the finding of the Claims Tribunal holding the appellant liable for payment of total compensation is just and proper and requires no interference in the same.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16965 6.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. It is a case of head on collision between two motorcycles.
One motorcycle i.e. M-1 was being driven by Baldev Kewat and Uttam @ Rajesh Sahu was sitting on it as a pillion rider.
Another motorcycle i.e. M-2 was being driven by Mahettar @ Bakra Sawra.
The drivers of both the motorcycles and the pillion rider died in the said accident.

The wife, children and parents of deceased Uttam @ Rajesh Sahu preferred an application registered as Claim Case No.121/2014 before the Claims Tribunal and against the award passed in the said Claim Case, the present appeal i.e. MAC No.1218/2015 has been preferred.

The claimants of deceased Baldev Prasad Kewat preferred an application registered as Claim Case No.122/2014 before the Tribunal and against the award passed in the said Claim Case, MAC No.1219/2015 has been preferred.
Both the claim applications were preferred against the driver/owner and insurance company of M-2.

Since the driver/ owner of M-2 namely Mahettar @ Bakra Sawra also died in the said accident, considering his wife Smt. Sadhna Bai as the owner, she has been arrayed as respondent in both the claim cases.

Taking into consideration the evidence available on record, the Tribunal passed the impugned award against the driver/owner and insurance company of M-2 and in favour of the claimants in respect of M-1.
Since the driver/owner also died in the said accident, the total liability came upon the insurance company of M-2.
It is this fastening of liability upon the insurance company against which this appeal has been preferred.
8. So far as the first ground of challenge that the driver of M-2 did not have a driving licence is concerned, the insurance company has not presented any evidence in this regard.

The burden of proving this fact is upon the insurance company but the insurance company has not produced any evidence in respect of breach of Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16965 policy conditions nor has any notice been issued to the driver or his legal representative to produce driving licence.
No such charge sheet has been filed in this case, so that it can be known whether the driver had a driving license at the time of the accident or not.
As such, the insurance company has not been able to establish by leading any cogent evidence that at the time of accident M-2 was being driven by Mahettar in violation of insurance policy conditions.
Thus, the breach of policy conditions is not found to be proved.

sentences.text: As regards the second ground of challenge regarding contributory negligence, on account of death of the drivers of both the motorcycles, FIRs have been lodged against them but no charge sheet has been filed in either case as both the drivers died in the accident.
In both the cases closure report (Khatma) has been filed.
From the investigation of Police it has not been proved that on whose rash and negligent driving the accident took place.
In the evidence that has been presented in the claim cases, the wives of the deceased are the witnesses but they were not present at the spot.
One Manoj Jaiswal who has been examined as a witness has accepted that he was not present at the spot.

As such, regarding rash and negligent driving, neither any statement of the spot witness has come on record nor has any charge sheet been filed by the Police showing that the particular person or driver or vehicle is responsible for the accident.

10. In such a situation, when the Tribunal itself has not been able to conclude on what basis it considers negligence only on the part of Mahettar i.e. the owner/driver of M-2, the Insurance Company of M-2 cannot be held liable for payment of total compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
When the motorcycles had a head-on collision, the drivers of both the motorcycles should be held responsible to have contributed equally to the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:16965 accident.

Therefore, there is a contributory negligence of 50% on the part of the driver of M-1.
11.

In that view of the matter, this Court is of the opinion that fastening of the entire liability on the motorcycle insured with the appellant herein is incorrect and it is held that the appellant is liable for payment of only 50% of the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal in Claim Case No.121/2014.
Thus, the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal vide impugned award dated 27.07.2015 is not disturbed.

However, the amount shall be paid by the appellant insurance company to the claimants to the extent of only 50% of the amount awarded by the Tribunal as the liability is apportioned on the motorcycle insured with the appellant to the extent of 50%.
Rest of the conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
12. Accordingly, this appeal of the insurance company is partly allowed to the extent indicated hereinabove.
